transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-07-07
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes (approx)
Recording: Yes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Maya Patel (Redwood SE), Samir Banerjee (CTO, Archipelago), Priya Kapoor (ML Eng), Liam O'Reilly (Infra), Hannah Cho (Security)

Summary: quick discovery to understand Archipelago's production model serving constraints and whether Redwood hosted, dedicated or private makes sense. They are currently on a mix of OpenAI (chat) and a vLLM/TGI self-hosted stack for embeddings & generation. Primary concerns: latency tail, cold-starts, cost predictability, SOC2 + KMS, ability to run private on-prem later.

Topics covered:
- Current architecture and pain points (OpenAI + in-house vLLM/TGI hybrid)
- Evaluation parity -> how Redwood verifies model outputs match their baseline
- Hosting options: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC/on-prem)
- Security controls: SSO, SAML, KMS, audit logs, data residency
- Benchmarking plan and next steps

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Lee: hey everyone thanks for joining, um we got about 50 minutes, hey Samir, Priya, Liam, Hannah, thanks for taking the time. quick intros?
[00:12] Samir Banerjee: yeah thanks Jordan, I'm Samir, CTO. Priya here runs the ml stack day to day, Liam owns infra, Hannah handles security reviews. we had a pretty brief agenda sent over, just wanna see fit.
[00:25] Jordan Lee: perfect, Maya and I will do a quick lit on Redwood and then dig into your stack and constraints — especially the vllm/TGI pieces you mentioned in the form.
[00:36] Maya Patel: hey all, I'm Maya, the solutions engineer. I focus on perf and private deploys, happy to sketch benchmarking and what parity checks look like.
[00:45] Priya Kapoor: awesome. quick disclosure, our stack today — we use OpenAI for chat and safety filters but for embeddings and most generation we run an internal setup: vLLM fronting TGI-based models on a fleet of gpus. it's been fine but we get weird latency spikes and the ops overhead is growing.
[01:05] Liam O'Reilly: yep, the cold-start kv cache problem and pre-allocation has been our headache. also, quantization variance between our dev and prod builds causes output drift sometimes.
[01:16] Hannah Cho: security-wise we need to keep data within our VPC and the ability to encrypt with our KMS; SOC2 is mandatory for sales ops.
[01:25] Jordan Lee: got it, thanks. curious, where would you rank the primary decision drivers — latency, cost, or ops lift?
[01:33] Samir Banerjee: latency tail and predictability first, then cost, then reducing ops lift. but compliance is a hard gate for some enterprise customers so VPC/KMS matters.
[01:45] Maya Patel: that maps with others we've seen. Redwood can do hosted API right away, dedicated reserved pools if you want predictable throughput, and private deployment for VPC/on-prem. can i ask about your throughput profile — typical qps and token distribution?
[02:00] Priya Kapoor: average 15 qps for embeddings during daytime peak, generation calls are spiky — p50 is ~120ms but p95 goes to 900ms sometimes and that spikes costs. token lengths vary widely, most are 32-256 tokens but we do some longform at 1k tokens.
[02:18] Maya Patel: okay long tails make sense with kv cache eviction. our serving runtime has continuous batching and prefix caching; for dedicated we pin warmed workers per model to reduce that cold-start.
[02:30] Liam O'Reilly: how different are your warmed vs cold resource costs? we want to avoid paying to keep huge numbers of gpus idle.
[02:38] Jordan Lee: good question. with Dedicated you get reserved capacity guarantees and can configure burst vs baseline. you can set autoscaling policies that keep a small pool warmed and allow burst into broader capacity as needed. pricing shows the delta; we'll send details.
[02:53] Samir Banerjee: on the eval side — we need output parity with our current TGI runs. we have an eval harness with a set of golden prompts and numeric metrics. how do you ensure you match model outputs?
[03:05] Maya Patel: parity is twofold — model matching and tokenizer/decoder differences. we support running identical model checkpoints where possible, and we provide quantization recommendations. but sometimes differences come from kernel-level rounding. we do regression testing against your harness and compute per-response diffs, token-level diffs, and human evals when needed.
[03:23] Priya Kapoor: do you support running TGI artifacts directly or do we need to re-export to a different format?
[03:29] Maya Patel: we can ingest standard model artifacts, but we usually recompile for our runtime to select optimized kernels. for TGI-vllm artifacts there are often small conversion steps; we've automated most of that.
[03:40] Hannah Cho: on security, can you run private control plane with our KMS? we need HSM-backed keys for certain customers. also audit logs retention is important.
[03:50] Jordan Lee: yes — Private deploy supports customer-managed KMS/HSM integrations and audit logs with configurable retention. for Hosted we offer bring-your-own-key patterns for certain enterprise plans.
[04:00] Liam O'Reilly: what's the network topology for Private? we want to avoid any outbound egress to public internet from the model runtime.
[04:08] Maya Patel: private can be deployed in your VPC with no public egress, or on-prem air-gapped if required. the control plane for Private can be run in a customer-managed manner; we provide the orchestration artifacts and a hardened runtime.
[04:20] Samir Banerjee: great. let's talk cost — currently our self-host is cheaper per-token but ops overhead is 3 FTEs. hosted is easier but worried about per-token volatility with OpenAI prices. how does Redwood compare economically?
[04:34] Jordan Lee: Redwood focuses on cost-aware controls — batching, KV caching, quantization profiles. for Dedicated we show unit economics closer to self-host with much less ops. we can model your current spend if you share sample traces.
[04:46] Priya Kapoor: ok we'll share traces but redactions — can you sign an NDA or are they okay with obfuscated data?
[04:53] Jordan Lee: we can take obfuscated traces first; if needed we have an NDA template and SOC2 controls already in the security pack.
[04:59] Hannah Cho: on compliance, do you have ISO or SOC2? and do you support SAML / enterprise SSO?
[05:06] Maya Patel: SOC2 Type II report available for Hosted and Dedicated; Private comes with a guidance pack for audits. SAML/SSO and fine-grained RBAC are supported. we'll put links in the pack.
[05:16] Samir Banerjee: about benchmarking — can Redwood run our benchmarks against hosted first and then Dedicated, so we can compare p95 tail and cost?
[05:24] Maya Patel: yes that's a typical path. hosted quickstart for initial eval, then dedicated reserved pool for a production-ish benchmark, and Private if you need VPC. for hosted you get immediate access to run your set, we just need sample keys and the prompts.
[05:36] Liam O'Reilly: any caveats for running long-form 1k token jobs at scale? memory usage and gradient-like operations?
[05:43] Maya Patel: for long sequences we have memory-optimized kernels and kv cache sharding. for 1k tokens we often recommend specific quantization and batch sizing; we'll propose config tuned to your distribution. also we can route long vs short requests to different instance types to be cost-effective.
[05:57] Priya Kapoor: about model mismatch — we saw different hallucination patterns when trying different quant levels. does Redwood offer controlled A/B or fallback to higher-fidelity models?
[06:07] Jordan Lee: yes, rollouts support canary and A/B tests, and automatic fallback policies to more accurate models if quality drops. Optimize gives suggestions for quantization vs quality tradeoffs.
[06:16] Samir Banerjee: what's the usual migration timeline if we go from hybrid to Dedicated? weeks, months?
[06:21] Maya Patel: typical pilot is 4–8 weeks including parity/eval and a small production cutover. full migration depends on scale and compliance gating — sometimes 3 months for enterprise customers.
[06:32] Priya Kapoor: we want deterministic reproducibility for audits. do you store model hashes and inference parameters per request?
[06:40] Maya Patel: yes, request-level metadata, model versions, config, and seed values are captured in audit logs. for Private you can retain logs for the retention window you configure.
[06:49] Hannah Cho: any customers doing air-gapped on-prem deployments with HSM? curious for references.
[06:55] Jordan Lee: a few financial and health customers — we'll include anonymized reference notes in the pack.
[07:02] Samir Banerjee: okay walk me through a minimal pilot: what do you need from us?
[07:08] Maya Patel: sample prompt set + evaluation metrics + redacted request traces + access pattern (qps). we stand up a host environment, run baseline on your harness, and compare p50/p95 and token cost; then we optimize batching/kv settings.
[07:21] Priya Kapoor: for the sample harness, do you run our exact golden models or are there conversion differences?
[07:27] Maya Patel: we try to run the same checkpoint where license allows; otherwise we match model family and reproduce tokenizer behavior as closely as possible. we report diffs and provide human-in-the-loop evaluations if needed.
[07:36] Liam O'Reilly: re: telemetry, what telemetry gets back to Redwood in Hosted? we need to know PII/time series etc.
[07:44] Jordan Lee: for Hosted we collect operational telemetry and aggregate usage; you can opt into anonymized or no-telemetry for an enterprise plan. Private gives full control — telemetry stays in your environment.
[07:54] Samir Banerjee: any surprises for us when converting vLLM/TGI pipelines?
[07:59] Maya Patel: the common surprises are tokenizer tokenization differences and attention-optimizer mismatch. those are usually fixed by a conversion step and a short calibration. we've seen rare cases where custom kernels were in play — then it's an engineering task but doable.
[08:12] Priya Kapoor: what's the cost/time to do the conversion step? just ballpark.
[08:16] Maya Patel: typical conversion + validation is 1–2 engineer-weeks for a standard model; if there are custom kernels add time. we estimate in the pilot.
[08:24] Samir Banerjee: ok that seems reasonable. can we get a short security doc now?
[08:28] Jordan Lee: yes, Maya will attach SOC2 excerpt, network diagrams, and KMS notes.
[08:34] Hannah Cho: also we need to see how RBAC maps to our internal roles.
[08:38] Maya Patel: we support role mapping via SAML groups and custom roles. we'll include an RBAC sample mapping doc.
[08:44] Priya Kapoor: last question — are there any hard limits on model size or custom ops in Private?
[08:50] Maya Patel: Private can be tailored, but very large custom ops may require additional engineering. model size limits are driven by hardware; we support sharded runtimes for big models.
[08:59] Jordan Lee: excellent. quick recap of next steps: we'll send pricing + pilot plan + security pack; you (Archipelago) will share sample traces and prompt sets; then we'll schedule the benchmark window. anything else?
[09:12] Samir Banerjee: please include a cost model comparing current infra vs dedicated vs hosted at our throughput.
[09:18] Jordan Lee: will do. thanks everyone, we'll follow up with an email and the pack.
[09:24] Priya Kapoor: thanks, appreciate it.
[09:26] Meeting end.
